answer: Auditors arrive in pairs each epoch. The protocol draws a square-root sample of established seats, and each auditor inspects two identities drawn at random from the whole population; a pair sharing attestors or funding lineage is reported jointly and its whole cluster loses standing. A farm of n names meets about n squared over twice N to the three-halves internal comparisons per epoch, so exposure climbs with size while a lone newcomer on the dune faces the base rate. The opal ledger records collided pairs permanently, so a terrace of ten identities grows riskier with each clone added.
